drivingQuestion: Why does R' Shimon need to say 'to what is this similar'?
outcomeNote: the Rabbis distinguish by the number of residents

segments.he: הָכִי קָאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן: מִכְּדִי לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה, לְשָׁלֹשׁ חֲצֵירוֹת הַפְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ, וּפְתוּחוֹת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דִּפְלִיגִיתוּ, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּלָא פְּלִיגִיתוּ?
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «This is what Rabbi Shimon said to the Rabbis: After all, to what is this similar? To three courtyards that open into one another, and that» also «open into a public domain. What is different there that you disagree» with me and say that it is prohibited to carry from any one courtyard to any other, «and what is different here that you do not disagree» with me?

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן: הָתָם אָוְושִׁי דָּיוֹרִין. הָכָא לָא אָוְושִׁי דָּיוֹרִין.
segments.en: «And» how do «the Rabbis» reply? «There» the «residents» of the courtyards «are numerous,» and some might come to carry objects in a place where it is prohibited to do so; whereas «here» the «residents are not numerous,» and a mere three people can warn each other against Shabbat desecration.
